test_title: PYST 72: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

We look forward to meet (1) / you at the orientation session (2) / scheduled for next Tuesday (3) / in the seminar hall. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is located in **part (1)** of the sentence: "**We look forward to meet**."
 
• The phrase "**look forward to**" is a phrasal verb where "**to**" functions as a **preposition**, not as part of an infinitive (to + verb).
 
• In English grammar, a preposition must be followed by a noun, a pronoun, or a **gerund** (the -ing form of a verb).
 
• Therefore, the base verb "**meet**" must be changed to the gerund "**meeting**" to be grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We **look forward to meeting** you at the orientation session scheduled for next Tuesday in the seminar hall."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(2): "you at the orientation session"** – This part is correct; it identifies the object and the specific event.
 
• **(3): "scheduled for next Tuesday"** – This part is correct; "scheduled" acts as a past participle modifying the session.
 
• **(4): "in the seminar hall"** – This is a correct prepositional phrase indicating the location.
 
• Other common phrases that follow this rule (Preposition 'to' + Gerund) include: *Object to, With a view to, Accustomed to, Used to.*
